newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end sharply lower in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end sharply lower in heavy trade.

text.p: Madrid share indices closed sharply lower on Wednesday, dragged by substantial falls in stocks that have outperformed in the last few sessions and amid losses on other European bourses, dealers said.
The general index fell 5.12 points, 1.05 percent, to 482.93 and the Ibex slipped 65.55 points, 1.17 percent, to 5,537.55.
Losses were concentrated in Endesa, down 230 pesetas to 9,180, Telefonica, which shed 50 pesetas to 3,485 and Santander which was off 220 pesetas to 9,640.
But today's losses, however acute, were qualified as technical after recent gains and amid some nerves in a volatile market.
The focus is now on Thursday's February consumer price index, seen up about 0.2 percent on the month for a 2.7/2.8 percent gain year on year, versus 2.9 percent in January.
But these figures would prompt more selling in the bourse, dealers said, as they would confirm the expected trend.
The figures may give room for a rate cut at the Bank of Spain's regular repo auction on Friday, some consider.
But a more cautious element of the market thinks the central bank will hold off because the peseta is not stable enough.
